title: Best Diving Spots in Jeddah 2026: Ranked Guide
body_markdown:
Jeddah's Red Sea coastline holds some of Saudi Arabia's best-known dive sites, and picking the right one in 2026 comes down to matching your certification level and tolerance for current to the reef in front of you.


**TL;DR**

- Shark Bay (Sharm Obhur) is the best overall pick among diving spots jeddah has to offer in 2026, with reef life close to shore.
- Um Al Birak suits advanced divers chasing drift dives along a pinnacle wall.
- Bayada Island is the easiest Jeddah water outing for beginners, snorkelers and mixed family groups.
- Marina House Reef needs no boat, making it the most convenient shore-entry option.
- Water across these diving spots jeddah runs 24-29°C year-round, with visibility of 20-30 meters most months.




## Why this matters

Searches for diving spots jeddah keep climbing as Saudi Arabia's tourism visa rules stay open to international divers who once flew straight past the kingdom on the way to Hurghada or Sharm el-Sheikh. Jeddah sits on the same Red Sea system, so the reef geology, coral cover and water clarity aren't a guess — they follow the same structure that built Egypt's dive reputation across the strait.

If you've never clipped on a regulator, the [scuba diving in Jeddah for beginners](https://dailyredsea.com/blog/scuba-diving-in-jeddah-for-beginners) guide walks through what a first dive actually involves before you commit to a site. Beyond the reef, [the best things to do in Jeddah](https://dailyredsea.com/blog/best-things-to-do-in-jeddah) rounds out a trip that isn't only underwater, which matters if you're traveling with people who won't be diving.

Visibility across these sites typically runs 20 to 30 meters, and the water holds 24-29°C year-round, so a 3mm wetsuit covers most of the calendar. That's close enough to Egyptian Red Sea norms that divers who've logged tanks in Hurghada or Marsa Alam will find the conditions familiar on arrival in 2026.

## What makes the best diving spots in Jeddah

- **Visibility and clarity** — how consistently the water stays clear across seasons, not just on a calm day
- **Reef health and coral cover** — live hard coral versus bleached or damaged sections
- **Shore access versus boat-only entry** — whether you need a charter or can walk straight in
- **Current strength and required certification** — some sites demand advanced or drift certification before booking
- **Marine life density** — reef fish, turtles and the occasional pelagic sighting
- **Distance from central Jeddah** — how much of your day gets eaten by transit

## Jeddah diving spots at a glance

| Site | Best For | Standout Feature | Key Limitation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Shark Bay (Sharm Obhur) | Best overall | Reef flat close to the beach | Gets crowded with day-trip groups |
| Seven Sisters | Best for reef variety | Seven reef heads in one dive | Boat-only access |
| Um Al Birak | Best for advanced/drift divers | Current-driven pinnacle wall | Current unsuitable for new divers |
| Bayada Island | Best for beginners and families | Shallow, calm snorkel water | Little depth for certified diving |
| Marina House Reef | Best for shore-entry | No boat needed, walk-in access | Lower marine life density |

## 1. Shark Bay (Sharm Obhur): best diving spot in Jeddah for first-time visitors

Sharm Obhur's Shark Bay is a wide, sheltered inlet north of central Jeddah where the reef starts a few meters from the sand and slopes gently before dropping toward open water. The name refers to the shape of the bay rather than resident sharks — sightings here are rare. It's the site most dive centers default to for a first dive of a 2026 trip because logistics are simple and the reef doesn't demand advanced skills.

**Shark Bay pros:**
- Reef starts close enough to shore for an easy check dive
- Consistent visibility across most months
- Full range of dive centers operate here, so booking an English-speaking guide is straightforward

**Shark Bay cons:**
- Weekend crowds mean multiple groups often share the same reef section
- Less current-driven marine action than sites further offshore

**Best for:** the first dive of a trip or a refresher after time out of the water.
**Verdict: Dive it** — the default pick for anyone unsure where to start.

## 2. Seven Sisters: best diving spot in Jeddah for reef variety

Seven distinct reef heads sit close together at this boat-only site, covering hard coral gardens, sandy channels and small overhangs without a long surface swim between them. It sits further offshore than Shark Bay, which trims the crowd but adds a longer boat ride.

**Seven Sisters pros:**
- Multiple reef structures covered in a single dive
- Solid macro life in the channels between reef heads
- Calmer current than Um Al Birak, suited to intermediate divers

**Seven Sisters cons:**
- Boat-only access adds a surface interval before you're in the water
- Depth varies sharply between reef heads, so buoyancy control matters

**Best for:** certified divers who want variety without technical current work.
**Verdict: Dive it** with open-water certification; **skip** it on a single-tank beginner trip.

## 3. Um Al Birak: best diving spot in Jeddah for advanced and drift divers

Um Al Birak is a pinnacle reef dropping into a wall, with current running along it strongly enough that most dive centers require advanced certification before booking a slot. Drift diving here covers more reef per tank than a stationary site allows, and the current brings in larger sightings more consistently than the sheltered spots closer to shore.

**Um Al Birak pros:**
- Genuine wall diving with real depth and structure
- Current brings pelagic sightings more often than calmer sites
- Drift profile covers more ground per dive

**Um Al Birak cons:**
- Current strength rules out first-time divers entirely
- Weather-dependent — rough conditions cancel the trip outright

**Best for:** divers holding drift or advanced open-water certification.
**Verdict: Dive it** if certified for current; **wait** if you haven't logged dives beyond open water.

## 4. Bayada Island: best diving spot in Jeddah for beginners and families

Bayada Island sits close enough to the mainland for a short boat hop, with shallow, calm water better suited to snorkeling and shore-style diving than deep exploration. It reads more as a beach day trip than a hardcore dive site, which is exactly why it works when the group includes non-divers.

If you're weighing whether the trip out is worth the time, [is Bayada Island worth visiting](https://dailyredsea.com/blog/is-bayada-island-jeddah-worth-visiting) breaks down what the island offers beyond the water.

**Bayada Island pros:**
- Calm, shallow water suited to snorkelers and non-divers in the same group
- Short boat ride from Jeddah's marina
- Sandy bottom is forgiving for first fin kicks

**Bayada Island cons:**
- Limited depth for divers chasing wall or drift profiles
- Marine life density trails the offshore reef sites

**Best for:** mixed groups with snorkelers, non-divers and kids.
**Verdict: Book it** for a family day; **skip** if you're diving solo and chasing depth.

## 5. Marina House Reef: best diving spot in Jeddah for shore-entry diving

Marina House Reef is reachable by walking straight off the beach near Jeddah's marina district, with no boat charter required. It's shallower and calmer than the boat-only sites, which makes it the go-to for a quick dive squeezed between other plans in 2026.

**Marina House Reef pros:**
- Shore entry cuts out boat logistics entirely
- Easy to dive with just a buddy, no group boat schedule to match
- Useful for buoyancy checks and gear tests before a bigger trip

**Marina House Reef cons:**
- Reef health and fish density trail the boat-only sites
- Shore traffic and boat wakes reduce visibility on busy days

**Best for:** a low-effort dive without booking a boat slot.
**Verdict: Dive it** for convenience; **skip** it if reef quality is your priority.

## How we ranked

Each site was weighed against the same six criteria: visibility, reef health, access type, current strength against certification level, marine life density and distance from central Jeddah. Shark Bay wins overall because it clears every criterion without demanding advanced skills. Um Al Birak and Seven Sisters score higher on marine life and structure but cost more in logistics or current exposure. Bayada Island and Marina House Reef rank lower on raw reef quality but win on access, which is exactly why they hold distinct "best for" slots instead of competing head-to-head with the boat-only sites.

## Which diving spot in Jeddah should you choose?

**Shark Bay (Sharm Obhur) is the default pick** if you only have one dive booked in 2026 and want the least friction between landing and being in the water. Certified divers chasing current and structure should book Um Al Birak; groups mixing divers with snorkelers or kids do best splitting time between Bayada Island and a boat dive at Shark Bay or Seven Sisters on the same trip.

If you're flexible on destination rather than locked into Jeddah, it's worth knowing the same Red Sea system runs down through Egypt, where the dive scene has been running longer and English-speaking operators are easier to find per site. Daily Red Sea runs its scuba and snorkeling trips out of Hurghada, on water with the same 24-29°C range and similar reef structure, without the added step of researching Saudi dive center logistics from scratch.

## FAQ


**What's the best diving spot in Jeddah?**

Shark Bay (Sharm Obhur) is the best overall diving spot in Jeddah for 2026, with reef access close enough to shore for a quick check dive and consistent visibility most of the year. Advanced divers chasing current and wall structure should book Um Al Birak instead.

**Is Jeddah good for beginner divers?**

Yes — Bayada Island and Shark Bay both offer shallow, sheltered water suited to first dives or refreshers. Um Al Birak's current makes it unsuitable until you've logged dives beyond open-water certification.

**Do you need certification to dive in Jeddah?**

Most dive centers in Jeddah require at least open-water certification for boat dives, and advanced certification for current sites like Um Al Birak. Shore dives at spots like Marina House Reef are more flexible for supervised beginners.

**Is Bayada Island worth visiting for snorkeling?**

Bayada Island suits snorkelers and mixed groups thanks to shallow, calm water close to shore, though it offers little for divers chasing depth or wall structure. It works best paired with a boat dive at a deeper site the same day.

**How does diving in Jeddah compare to diving in Hurghada?**

Jeddah and Hurghada sit on the same Red Sea system, so reef structure, water temperature and visibility read similarly on a dive computer. Hurghada's dive scene, including operators like Daily Red Sea, has been running longer with more English-speaking centers per site.

**What's the water temperature for diving in Jeddah?**

Red Sea water temperature runs 24-29°C (75-84°F) across the year, consistent for both the Jeddah and Egyptian coastlines. A 3mm wetsuit covers most months and a shorty is enough at peak summer.

**Are there wreck dives near Jeddah?**

The named dive sites covered here are reef and wall dives rather than wrecks — Um Al Birak and Seven Sisters are reef-based, not sunken vessels. Divers specifically chasing wreck diving typically look toward Egypt's Red Sea coast instead.

**What's the best time of year to dive in Jeddah?**

Diving is possible year-round given the 24-29°C water temperature range, though summer months bring the warmest water and calmest surface conditions for boat access to sites like Seven Sisters.


## One last thing

Jeddah's reef sites see noticeably less boat traffic than Hurghada's reefs on a busy Saturday, largely because Saudi Arabia only opened broadly to international tourism in recent years compared to Egypt's decades-old dive industry. That gap works in your favor in 2026 if quiet reef time matters more to you than choice of operators — just don't expect the same density of dive shops per site that you'd find across the strait.
